subtitle: When the Kushan Mint Hammered the Names of Many Gods into Gold

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a Kushan mint hall as coins gleam in the lamplight
panels.action: The Kushan Mint Master stands amid furnaces and anvils, holding a freshly struck gold dinar up to the glow, its tiny deity figure catching the firelight in the bustling imperial workshop.

dialogue.text: In the age of Kanishka and the Kushans, coins became little temples of empire, carrying thirty gods across Bactria, Gandhara, Kapisa and Mathura.

i18n.hi: कनीष्क और कुशानों के युग में सिक्के छोटे मंदिर बने, जो बाख़्त्रिया, गांधार, कपीसा और मथुरा में तीस देवता लिए घूमते थे।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the Central Asian steppe fading into river valleys and caravan roads
panels.action: A sweeping landscape shows wind-blown steppe, the Oxus river, and caravan trails threading south towards the lush valleys of Gandhara and the crowded markets of Mathura.

dialogue.text: From the cold plains of Bactria to the warm stone ghats of Mathura, the Kushan empire sat astride the Silk Road, binding traders, pilgrims and soldiers into one hard web of power.

i18n.hi: ठंडी बाख़्त्रिया से गरम मथुरा के घाटों तक, कुशन साम्राज्य रेशम मार्ग पर जकड़ा था, जो व्यापारियों, यात्रियों और सैनिकों को ताकत के जाल में बाँधता था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a bustling market, focus on hands passing coins
panels.action: In a crowded Gandharan bazaar, the Kushan Mint Master moves through the throng, watching Indian merchants, Iranian horsemen and Greek-speaking traders as coins change hands atop cloth-covered stalls.

dialogue.text: In these markets, the empire was not a proclamation. It was weight in the palm, the glitter of gold and copper stamped with kings, scripts and gods from many lands.

i18n.hi: इन बाज़ारों में साम्राज्य कोई फ़रमान नहीं था, बल्कि हथेली की ठोस क़ीमत था—सोने, ताँबे की चमक, जिस पर अलग-अलग देसों के राजा, लिपियाँ और देवता खुदे थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a Kushan gold coin between fingers, obverse showing king standing
panels.action: Fingers hold a Kushan gold dinar close: on one side the standing Kushan king in long coat and boots, sacrificing at an altar; Greek letters curve along the rim in the Bactrian tongue.

dialogue.text: The obverse showed the king, often Kanishka, in Central Asian dress, naming himself in Bactrian, written with Greek letters, as rightful lord over these mingled peoples.

i18n.hi: सिक्के के सामने की तरफ़ राजा, अक्सर कनीष्क, मध्य एशियाई पोशाक में दिखता, बैक्ट्रियन भाषा में, ग्रीक अक्षरों से, अपने को मिली-जुली जनता का वैध स्वामी कहता था।

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up on coin reverse, deity figure and inscription
panels.action: The coin is flipped: a robust goddess figure stands frontal, arms outstretched, beside a vertical legend of angular Greek letters spelling a divine name in Bactrian.

dialogue.text: The reverse carried gods: Nana, Miiro, Aurmuzd, Ardoxsho, Buddha, Oesho, Serapis and many others, each named in Bactrian script, each chosen to speak to a different devotion.

i18n.hi: पीछे की तरफ़ देवता चलते थे: नाना, मीर्रो, औरमुज़्द, अर्दोक्षो, बुद्ध, ओएशो, सेरापिस और कई और, हर नाम बैक्ट्रियन लिपि में, हर देव अलग भक्ति से बात करता।

panels.shot: interior wide of a mint workshop with dies, molds and scribes at low tables
panels.action: In the imperial mint, artisans carve dies, weigh metal and consult wax tablets, while the Kushan Mint Master oversees, flanked by a scribe copying divine names in careful Greek letters.

dialogue.text: Here, in the beating heart of the mint, the masters married image and script, turning political calculation into sacred metal that could cross languages and borders.

i18n.hi: यहीं टकसाल की धड़कती धमन में उस्तादों ने चित्र और लिखावट की शादी करवाई, राजनीति को पवित्र धातु में ढाल दिया जो भाषाएँ और सरहदें पार कर सके।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mint Master conferring with a court official over pattern sheets
panels.action: The Kushan Mint Master and a court official bend over wax pattern sheets, each inscribed with different divine figures and legends, a map of the empire’s religious landscape laid out on a table.

dialogue.text: The kings wanted more than taxation. They wanted loyalty. Mint masters were ordered to show the patronage of many gods, so every subject might see their own divine ally beside the king’s fire.

i18n.hi: राजाओं को सिर्फ़ कर नहीं, निष्ठा चाहिए थी। टकसाल को हुक्म था कई देवताओं की छाया दिखाने का, ताकि हर प्रजा राजा की अग्नि के पास अपना देव साथी देख सके।

panels.shot: majestic wide of Kanishka at a ceremony, stylized and distant
panels.action: A stylized scene shows Kanishka standing on a raised platform before officials and artisans, gesturing towards wooden boards hung with sketches of royal and divine images.

dialogue.text: In the Rabatak inscription, Kanishka proclaimed his kingship came from Nana and all the gods, and ordered royal and divine images, making plural patronage part of state display.

i18n.hi: रबताक लेख में कनीष्क ने ऐलान किया कि उसका राज नाना और सब देवताओं से आया, और राजसी व दिव्य मूर्तियाँ बनवाने का आदेश दिया, ताकि बहु-देव संरक्षण राज की शान बन जाए।

panels.shot: close-up on Mint Master’s intent face lit by furnace glow
panels.action: The Kushan Mint Master stands near the furnace, his face lit in orange, eyes narrowed in thought as he imagines coins traveling from Bactria’s fortresses to Mathura’s shrines.

dialogue.speaker: Kushan Mint Master
dialogue.text: If each god stands on our coins, each city will feel the king’s hand.

i18n.hi: अगर हर देव हमारे सिक्कों पर खड़ा हो, तो हर नगर राजा का हाथ महसूस करेगा।

panels.shot: sequence-style wide with multiple sample coins laid out like a fan
panels.action: On a low table in the mint, a fan of different Kushan coins lies arranged: Nana seated on a lion, Miiro with rays, Ardoxsho holding cornucopia, Buddha standing, a debated Oesho-style figure with trident-like attributes.

dialogue.text: The range was astonishing. Iranian Nana and Aurmuzd, solar Miiro, prosperity Ardoxsho, Hellenistic Serapis, the Buddha, and more than thirty deities made up the imperial pantheon in metal.

i18n.hi: फ़ैला ऐसा था कि हैरत हो—ईरानी नाना और औरमुज़्द, तेजस वाला मीर्रो, समृद्धि की अर्दोक्षो, हेलनिस्टिक सेरापिस, बुद्ध, और तीस से ज़्यादा देवों ने धातु में साम्राज्य का देवसमूह रचा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mint Master instructing die engraver on a Buddha coin
panels.action: The Kushan Mint Master guides a die engraver’s hand over a wax blank, indicating the outline of a standing Buddha with monastic robe and halo, while the scribe notes the Bactrian legend.

dialogue.text: Buddha was one among many, honored on coins that also bore Nana and Aurmuzd. These issues showed patronage of Buddhist institutions, but not an exclusive conversion of the king.

i18n.hi: बुद्ध भी बस कई में एक थे, उन सिक्कों पर सम्मानित जो साथ में नाना और औरमुज़्द भी लिए थे। ये निर्गम बौद्ध संस्थानों की छत्रछाया दिखाते थे, पर राजा के किसी एक धर्म में ढल जाने का सबूत नहीं थे।

panels.shot: detail shot of die engraver working on an Oesho-like figure, Mint Master watching
panels.action: A die engraver carves a muscular, three-armed deity with uplifted weapon, while the Kushan Mint Master studies older dies and foreign models, uncertain how best to name this syncretic figure.

dialogue.text: Later scholars would debate Oesho: was it Vayu-Vata, a Shiva-like form, or a fusion? Even in the mint, deities could blur, carried between Iranian, Indian and local ways of seeing.

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वान ओएशो पर उलझे—क्या वो वायु-वात थे, शिव-से रूप या कोई मेल? खुद टकसाल में भी देवताएँ धुँधला सकती थीं, ईरानी, भारतीय और स्थानीय दृष्टियों के बीच बहती हुई।

panels.shot: wide of mint floor where different coin types are being struck in parallel
panels.action: Across the mint floor, workers strike different dies: one batch with Nana, another with Buddha, another with Ardoxsho, the rhythm of hammer blows echoing like a many-voiced chant.

dialogue.text: This was not modern tolerance. It was strategy: an empire speaking many sacred languages at once, so its authority could travel without translation from shrine to fire altar.

i18n.hi: ये आधुनिक सहिष्णुता नहीं थी, ये चाल थी—साम्राज्य एक साथ कई पवित्र भाषाएँ बोलता था, ताकि उसकी सत्ता बिना अनुवाद के देवालय से अग्निकुंड तक चल सके।

panels.shot: market montage wide showing diverse people examining different deity coins
panels.action: In a montage-like scene across the bazaar, a Buddhist monk, a Zoroastrian priest, a local goddess worshipper and a Greek-speaking merchant each holds a Kushan coin bearing their familiar deity.

dialogue.text: In Gandhara, Kapisa and Mathura, each devotee could find their god on imperial money, seeing their faith recognized, yet always paired with the Kushan king’s unshaken stance.

i18n.hi: गांधार, कपीसा और मथुरा में हर भक्त अपने देव को राजसी सिक्कों पर देख सकता था, अपना धर्म मान्यता पाता हुआ, पर हर बार कुशन राजा की अडोल मुद्रा के साथ जोड़ा हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up of scribe copying Bactrian text with Greek letters onto a tablet
panels.action: A scribe in the mint carefully copies the name ‘Nana’ in Bactrian, using Greek letters on a wax tablet, as the Kushan Mint Master checks for accuracy before a new die is cut.

dialogue.text: Bactrian, written in Greek letters, carried these divine names. Later documents from northern Afghanistan would help scholars hear this language that once whispered on coins.

i18n.hi: बैक्ट्रियन, जो ग्रीक अक्षरों में लिखी जाती थी, इन्हीं देव नामों को ढोती थी। बाद में उत्तर अफ़गानिस्तान के दस्तावेज़ों ने विद्वानों को वो भाषा सुनने दी जो कभी सिक्कों पर फुसफुसाती थी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of coins traveling in caravans, then buried, then unearthed
panels.action: A visual sequence shows sacks of Kushan coins on camel caravans, then sealed in hoards beneath ruined walls, then centuries later emerging in an archaeologist’s gloved hand from dust.

dialogue.text: Empires fall. Roads fade. Yet in buried hoards and river sediments, these coins survived, their small gods and kings waiting for modern eyes to read their careful, multilingual claims.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य गिरते हैं, राहें मिटती हैं। पर दबे खज़ानों और नदी की परतों में ये सिक्के बचे रहे, अपने छोटे देव और राजाओं संग, आज की आँखों का इंतज़ार करते हुए कि कोई उनकी धीरज, बहुभाषी दावेदारी पढ़े।

panels.shot: modern museum-case style wide, Mint Master ghosted in background like memory
panels.action: A museum display holds rows of Kushan coins under glass, each labeled; behind them, faint and stylized, the Kushan Mint Master’s figure watches silently, as if his choices still echo.

dialogue.text: Numismatists like Jongeward, Cribb and Donovan counted more than thirty gods on Kushan issues, revealing how imperial patronage could be plural, calculated and precise.

i18n.hi: जोंगेवार्ड, क्रिब और डोनोवन जैसे मुद्राविदों ने कुशन सिक्कों पर तीस से ज़्यादा देव गिने, दिखाते हुए कि राजसी संरक्षण कितना बहु-देवी, सोचा-समझा और नपे-तुले अंदाज़ में चल सकता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up on a single coin reverse showing deity and legend
panels.action: A single Kushan coin lies isolated on a dark surface, reverse up, its deity sharply lit, its Bactrian legend clear, tiny yet firm against the surrounding shadow.

dialogue.text: The Kushan mint masters taught that respect can grow when power learns many gods by name, and that in the smallest coin, an empire’s idea of faith and rule can endure for ages.

i18n.hi: कुशन टकसाल उस्तादों ने सिखाया कि जब सत्ता कई देवताओं को नाम से जाने, तो सम्मान बढ़ सकता है, और सबसे छोटे सिक्के में भी साम्राज्य की आस्था और राज की कल्पना सदियों तक टिक सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Kushan Mint Hammered the Names of Many Gods into Gold
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब कुशन टकसाल ने कई देवताओं के नाम सोने पर जड़ दिए
